source.original_text: Let \(A,B\) be arbitrary measurable spaces, \(\mu\) an s-finite measure on \(A\), \(R:A\rightsquigarrow B\) an s-finite kernel, and \(F:A\times B\rightsquigarrow B\) a jointly measurable s-finite kernel. Suppose that, for \(\mu\)-almost every \(a\), the kernel \(F_a(b,\cdot)=F((a,b),\cdot)\) is reversible under \(R(a,\cdot)\), in the sense of equality of nonnegative fluxes between every pair of measurable subsets of \(B\). Put \(\nu(da,db)=\mu(da)R(a,db)\). Then the transition \(L((a,b),d(a\prime,b\prime))=\delta_a(da\prime)F((a,b),db\prime)\), which retains the first coordinate, is reversible under \(\nu\). Neither the measures nor the kernels need be normalized or finite; zero measures, empty spaces and infinite fluxes are allowed.

    {A B : Type*} [MeasurableSpace A] [MeasurableSpace B]
    (μ : Measure A) [SFinite μ]
    (R : Kernel A B) [IsSFiniteKernel R]
    (F : Kernel (A × B) B) [IsSFiniteKernel F]
    (hF : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, (F.comap (fun b => (a, b))
      (measurable_const.prodMk measurable_id)).IsReversible (R a)) :
    ((Kernel.deterministic Prod.fst measurable_fst) ×ₖ F).IsReversible (μ ⊗ₘ R)
decoder_context: Kernel X Y is a measurable map to nonnegative measures: for every measurable S in Y, x maps to kappa(x)(S) measurably. No Markov or finite-mass premise is part of this type.
SFinite on a measure means it is a countable sum of finite measures. IsSFiniteKernel is the analogous countable-sum condition for kernels. Neither class asserts probability normalization.

For a measurable map g, kappa.comap g is the kernel x maps to kappa(g(x)). Kernel.deterministic g is x maps to dirac(g(x)). Kernel product gives the independent product of its two output measures at the same input.
For s-finite mu and R, mu compProd R is the measure integrating a joint nonnegative measurable f as the iterated integral of f(a,b) against R(a) then mu.

IsReversible kappa pi means: for every pair of measurable sets S,T, the nonnegative integral over S of kappa(x)(T) against pi equals the analogous integral over T of kappa(x)(S). The definition itself has no Markov premise.
The notation forall-a.e. uses the measure ae filter; output flux integrals are extended nonnegative integrals, not totalized real Bochner integrals.

import Mathlib.Probability.Kernel.Invariance
import Mathlib.Probability.Kernel.Composition.MeasureCompProd

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Filter
open scoped ENNReal

/-!
# Detailed balance for a retained-coordinate transition

Let the joint law be `μ ⊗ₘ R`. A jointly measurable update `F (a,b)` changes
only `b`. If the update on almost every fiber is reversible under `R a`, the
retained-coordinate joint transition is reversible under the joint law.

This is a canonical nonnegative-flux lemma, not a paper-specific process
construction. It allows s-finite measures and kernels, including zero/empty
cases and infinite fluxes. Markovness, normalization and finite mass are not
assumed. Invariance requires a separate Markov-kernel hypothesis.

Planned consumers: the actual PBPS half-turn adapter (arXiv:2609.06905v1,
Appendix A.2/A.9) and general component-wise Gibbs/heat-bath reversibility.
Disintegration, coordinate transport and the actual all-L2 operator remain
separate obligations. No source theorem or paper completion is claimed here.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.KernelRetainedReversibility

private theorem retained_flux
    {A B : Type*} [MeasurableSpace A] [MeasurableSpace B]
    (μ : Measure A) [SFinite μ]
    (R : Kernel A B) [IsSFiniteKernel R]
    (F : Kernel (A × B) B) [IsSFiniteKernel F]
    {S T : Set (A × B)} (hS : MeasurableSet S) (hT : MeasurableSet T) :
    (∫⁻ z in S, ((Kernel.deterministic Prod.fst measurable_fst) ×ₖ F) z T
      ∂(μ ⊗ₘ R)) =
    ∫⁻ a, ∫⁻ b in Prod.mk a ⁻¹' S, F (a, b) (Prod.mk a ⁻¹' T) ∂R a ∂μ := by
  rw [← lintegral_indicator hS]
  rw [Measure.lintegral_compProd
    ((((Kernel.deterministic Prod.fst measurable_fst) ×ₖ F).measurable_coe hT).indicator hS)]
  apply lintegral_congr
  intro a
  rw [← lintegral_indicator (hS.preimage measurable_prodMk_left)]
  apply lintegral_congr
  intro b
  by_cases hab : (a, b) ∈ S
  · rw [Set.indicator_of_mem hab,
      Set.indicator_of_mem (show b ∈ Prod.mk a ⁻¹' S from hab)]
    exact Kernel.deterministic_prod_apply' measurable_fst F (a, b) hT
  · rw [Set.indicator_of_notMem hab,
      Set.indicator_of_notMem (show b ∉ Prod.mk a ⁻¹' S from hab)]

/-- Almost-everywhere fiber detailed balance lifts to the transition which
retains the first coordinate. Joint measurability comes from the kernel `F`;
measurable joint sets have measurable fiber sections. All integrals are
nonnegative, so no finite-flux or integrability premise is needed. -/
theorem retained_coordinate_isReversible
    {A B : Type*} [MeasurableSpace A] [MeasurableSpace B]
    (μ : Measure A) [SFinite μ]
    (R : Kernel A B) [IsSFiniteKernel R]
    (F : Kernel (A × B) B) [IsSFiniteKernel F]
    (hF : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, (F.comap (fun b => (a, b))
      (measurable_const.prodMk measurable_id)).IsReversible (R a)) :
    ((Kernel.deterministic Prod.fst measurable_fst) ×ₖ F).IsReversible (μ ⊗ₘ R) := by
  intro S T hS hT
  rw [retained_flux μ R F hS hT, retained_flux μ R F hT hS]
  apply lintegral_congr_ae
  filter_upwards [hF] with a ha
  exact ha (hS.preimage measurable_prodMk_left) (hT.preimage measurable_prodMk_left)

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.KernelRetainedReversibility

Put \(\nu(da,db)=\mu(da)R(a,db)\). Then the transition \(L((a,b),d(a\prime,b\prime))=\delta_a(da\prime)F((a,b),db\prime)\), which retains the first coordinate, is reversible under \(\nu\). assumptions: A kernel includes genuine measurability for every measurable output set. Joint measurability of F is a real premise encoded by its type; separate fiber measurability would not suffice for the disintegration argument.

The s-finite assumptions select the meaningful pinned Mathlib compProd and kernel-product interfaces. They are not asserted to be logically minimal for every possible independently defined extension. Outside these classes, totalized zero defaults must not be used as mathematical evidence.

The fiber detailed-balance premise holds simultaneously for all measurable fiber sets outside one mu-null set. Its good set needs no separately supplied measurability certificate. Joint-set sections are measurable preimages, not projections.

No Markov, probability, finite-mass, sigma-finite, Standard-Borel, topology, measurable-singleton, nonempty or real-integrability premise is present. All flux integrals are nonnegative and may be infinite.

This shared theorem does not construct a paper-specific conditional law. An actual PBPS or Gibbs adapter must identify its SAME selected R and joint disintegration. Detailed balance alone, without Markovness, is not an invariance assertion.

steps.title: Disintegrate the flux through measurable sections
steps.text: Fix arbitrary measurable joint sets S,T, and define their sections S_a={b:(a,b) belongs to S} and T_a similarly. Each section is measurable because b maps to (a,b) measurably. The function z maps to L(z,T) is measurable since L is a kernel. Replace its restricted integral over S by the integral of the measurable indicator-weighted function. Nonnegative compProd integration then separates the retained coordinate a and the updated coordinate b. The deterministic first-coordinate kernel forces the new first coordinate to equal a, so L((a,b),T)=F((a,b),T_a). Restricting the inner integral to S_a gives exactly the displayed identity.
steps.detail: This step proves the formula for arbitrary joint sets, not only rectangles. The Lean helper uses lintegral_indicator and lintegral_compProd; the rectangular setLIntegral_compProd theorem is deliberately not used. In its last case split, membership in S and in S_a are definitionally the same condition.

steps.title: Apply fiber balance almost everywhere, then reassemble
steps.text: For almost every retained coordinate a, apply the assumed reversible-kernel equality to the measurable sets S_a and T_a. This equates the two inner fluxes. Equality almost everywhere suffices to equate their outer nonnegative integrals. Apply the previous disintegration identity once to S,T and once to T,S. The resulting equality is the definition of joint reversibility. No subtraction of infinite quantities and no exchange of signed integrals occurs.
steps.detail: In Lean, filter_upwards obtains a fiber satisfying detailed balance; the two measurable-preimage proofs make its section sets admissible. lintegral_congr_ae performs the outer integration. The public theorem does not add a pointwise reversibility or a Markov premise.
steps.lean:
intro S T hS hT
  rw [retained_flux μ R F hS hT, retained_flux μ R F hT hS]
  apply lintegral_congr_ae
  filter_upwards [hF] with a ha
  exact ha (hS.preimage measurable_prodMk_left) (hT.preimage measurable_prodMk_left)
